text:
joey: Heads-up — saw a tight cluster of midstream early-EOFs during the EU routing rollout at ~11:07. Clients reconnected and a few tenants got 1-2 extra token increments. Not widespread but reproducible.

alisa: Early-EOF meaning 499 from edge or proxy-level 204?

joey: A mix. Edge logs show 499 client_closed in a subset, proxy logs show 204 for lease-not-found. The billing stream shows duplicate increment_count events for the same session within 2s.

fran: Console traces? sampling level?

joey: Resume span sampling is low (0.5%) so traces are sparse. Pasted a short snippet to #platform-logs but here's the gist: client sees socket close -> immediate reconnect -> sends resume -> server processes attach -> client sends another resume almost immediately -> server processes again because attach idempotency relies on sticky lease which got dropped.

alisa: Oof. Which config rolled? the new fast-evict shard assignment?

joey: Yeah, the rollout tightened route-lease eviction to accelerate failover. That sped things up but exposed a small race between eviction and attach idempotency.

fran: Repro script (local):

```
# repro early-eof race
curl -N "https://api.redwood/stream?v=1&client=testx" &
sleep 1
# trigger route eviction quickly
curl -XPOST "https://console.internal/api/routes/evict?target=eu-canary&force=true"
sleep 0.5
# simulate client restart
kill -HUP $!; sleep 2
```

fran: I can reproduce two attach events hitting counting pipeline within 1-2s.

miko: Immediate mitigations we discussed: 1) pause the eviction tighten for canary (rollback to previous window), 2) bump resume span sampling to 15% for 6h so we can get good traces, 3) add a short-lived alert that pages SRE when resume_retries > 6/min AND billing_dup_events > 0.

joey: Also a medium-term fix: make proxy generate an X-Stream-Attempt header (stable per reattach attempt) and have the counting service treat identical X-Stream-Attempt as idempotent within a 3s TTL. That way rapid client retries won't double-increment.

alisa: I like X-Stream-Attempt (nonce), but let's make sure the header is derived from session_id+last_event_id+route_version so it's stable across retries but changes when client legitimately moves forward.

fran: Console UX ask: show a live annotation in the streaming dashboard when route eviction/lease changes are rolled. We spent time correlating by hand. A small badge on the timeline would help. Product agreed in principle but wants mockups.

miko: For immediate action I'll open a hotfix: routes.eviction_window.eu-canary=60000 (ms) and tracing.resume_sample=0.15. Rolling now.

deploy-bot: deploy-bot: Applying cfg-202478: routes.eviction_window.eu-canary=60000, tracing.resume_sample=0.15. Rolling: 1/3 hosts updated. Change-id cfg-202478.

ops-bot: ops-bot: Alert rule created: page SRE if (resume_retries > 6/min) AND (billing_duplicate_events >= 1) for 5m.

joey: After the eviction window increase + sampling bump we saw duplicate increments drop ~94% within 2 minutes. We still captured a couple of residual dup events while config rolled.

alisa: Follow-ups: TKT-237 implement-x-stream-attempt, TKT-238 normalize-route-quota-namespace-on-ingest, TKT-239 dashboard-rollout-annotations, TKT-240 postroll-sample-boost. Also add an ops playbook step to auto-boost streaming sampling for 24h after any topology or routing change.

fran: For the counting service design note: accept-first-wins semantics for identical X-Stream-Attempt within TTL, and emit an audit span when a duplicate is received (so we can instrument billing regressions).

miko: Agreed. I'll file the design doc and a small migration plan for existing routes to ensure quota_namespace is canonical across shards.

joey: Incident note: midstream early-EOFs + tight eviction rollout caused a small number of duplicate token increments; mitigated by increasing eviction window for canary, adding alerting, and boosting tracing sampling. Will follow with a short postmortem and PRs for nonce-based idempotency and dashboard annotations. :thumbsup:
